sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ARGUMENTS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Lingasugur (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.544/2018 vide its judgment and award dated 02.03.2020.
2.

The claimants are the dependant legal heirs of the deceased - Girijamma, who was aged 45 years and who died in a road traffic accident on 22.05.2017 involving Mini Bus in which she was traveling and lorry bearing registration No.KA- 48/3801 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle').
The claimants claimed that the deceased was working as a tailor and was earning a monthly income of Rs.15,000/-.

The claimants claimed that due to the death of Smt. Girijamma, they had lost her financial and emotional support and hence, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles NC: 2023:KHC-K:5564 Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer who denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimants for compensation.
It denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P8.

The insurer did not lead any evidence, but marked Ex.R1.
5.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle was rash and negligent and was solely responsible for the accident resulting in the death of Smt. Girijamma.

It held that the deceased was aged 45 years and considered her notional income at a sum of Rs.10,000/- and deducted 1/3rd towards her personal and living expenses and applied multiplier of '14' and awarded the following compensation:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Loss of dependency 11,20,056/-
Gangdhar Biradar W/O Basavantappa And ... vs Pavana Udapudi S/O Basavaraj And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98549135/
2  NC: 2023:KHC-K:5564  2 Loss of estate, loss of 70,000/-
 consortium and funeral  expenses  3 Loss of love and affection 1,00,000/-
 Total 12,96,723/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants are in appeal.
7.

The learned counsel for the claimants contended that, the Tribunal committed an error in considering the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month, while in similar circumstances, the notional income is considered at a sum of Rs.10,250/- per month.

He submitted that the Tribunal failed to factor the loss of future prospects at 25% as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further contended that the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5564 compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads was also meager and the same deserves to be enhanced.
8. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer of the offending vehicle contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.

10. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.10,250/- as per the Chart prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of dispute at Lok Adalat.
The claimants were also entitled to loss of future prospects at 25% of the income of the deceased.

11. Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5564 Sl. Particulars Amount No. (in Rs.) 1

Towards loss of dependency 14,35,056/- 2 Towards loss of consortium 40,000/- 3 Towards loss of estate, 70,000/-
Gangdhar Biradar W/O Basavantappa And ... vs Pavana Udapudi S/O Basavaraj And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98549135/
3 funeral expenses etc., Total 15,05,056/-
12.

Since the liability of the insurer of the offending vehicle is undisputed, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
13. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.12,96,723/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.15,05,056/-, which is payable by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
14.
The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant No.2 in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
